title: A dropped batch uploads small files first and no file waits behind a large file's slot wait
cause: docs/evidence/step-9/s9-6b/result.json: run 4 started files in drop order and retainBatch released the next file only once the one before it was admitted or stopped. The 12,063-byte GeoTIFF dropped last waited 123 s behind the second large GeoTIFF, which waited for the single v2 slot (open_receipts, maxActiveGlobal 1) held by the first.

change.startOrder: retain-batch.ts retainBatch starts files by ascending byte size (startOrder; the sort is stable, so equal sizes keep drop order). Rows, row indexes and outcomes keep drop order.
change.release: retain-batch.ts updateUpload releases the next file when this file's upload is stopped or waiting for a free upload slot (slotWait: either slot-wait words). The batch no longer paints the earlier-file words on files that have not asked for a slot; each command publishes its own wait.
change.slotLine: upload-command.ts slotLine is a Map of ticket to profile version; slotAhead(ticket, version) counts only earlier waiters for the same profile. Needed because the server counts v1 and v2 slots apart (large-original.ts quotaSql filters every held count by v2=$3); with one shared line a v2 file released by a v1 file's slot wait still waited behind it although the v2 slot was free (test 2 fails with retain-batch.ts changed alone).
change.unchanged: resume, retry, cancel, the stopped controls, the outcome rows, the 30-minute slot stop, the server, the contracts and the screens

added: upload.test.ts S9.6e: a batch shaped like run 4 (csv, large-1 v2, large-2 v2, small tif) is asked for in the order small tif, csv, large-2, large-1; rows stay in drop order; the small tif is enrolled while large-1 still waits for the v2 slot
upload.test.ts S9.6e: a v1 file waiting for a v1 case slot lets the later v2 file start, be admitted and finish at once; no row shows the earlier-file words
upload.test.ts S9.6e: three v2 files dropped largest first are admitted smallest first and keep their slot-line order; the third shows the earlier-file words, the second the server's slot words
adjusted: upload.test.ts FIFO batch admission: expects the start order first.csv, third.csv, second.tif, fourth.tif

retain-batch-part-failure.test.ts: the two later files are made larger than the failing file so it still starts first; a stopped file still releases the next (a refusal that stays ... releases the next files)
retain-batch.test.ts starts the next upload while a retained bounded file is still enrolling: next.csv made larger than the footprints file so the bounded file still starts first
tests.failOnBase: the three added tests fail on d39f438f; with only retain-batch.ts changed, the v1-slot-wait test still fails
